88604.title: Revenue and Billing Efficiency tiles show the right headline and line
88604.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You can switch to a busy location (workplace) that has invoices and technician clocked time over the last twelve months.
  4. The Dash Shop data set exists, all created today in location ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop, where nothing else is invoiced or clocked this month: work order 1 for customer ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.50 and technician ZZAUTOTEST Tech One, a part with Sell Price $50.00, and ZZAUTOTEST Tech One clocked exactly 2.50 hours on it; work order 2 for ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y, one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.00 and technicians ZZAUTOTEST Tech One and ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two, a part with Sell Price $160.00, Tech One clocked exactly 0.25 hours and Tech Two exactly 0.75 hours on it. Neither work order has shop supplies, a fee or a discount; both are invoiced and not paid. Totals: invoices $250.00 and $260.00; 3.00 labor hours billed; 2.50 technician hours on the lines; 3.50 clocked hours; no internal (non work order) time.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: on the Dashboard, switch the Revenue and Technician Efficiency pills to Last 12 Months: both show figures; then set both back to This Month (the dashboard remembers your choices in this browser). If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
  • For 4: if ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop already exists with exactly this data, reuse it. Otherwise: (a) location: profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop, the address fields, Timezone, Telephone, Shop Supplies Charge 0 % > Save & Close (if a location with this name already exists, reuse it only if it still matches the precondition). It then appears in your Change Location list; to switch to it, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. (b) staff: profile icon > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member, four times: ZZAUTOTEST Tech One and ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two with Role Technician and Time Clock on, ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X and ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y with Role Service Advisor; each with Location ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop and a Department > Save & Close. Give each technician an email address you can open: they must accept the invitation email and set a password so you can sign in as them in a private window. (c) customers: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save, for ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Fleet and ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet. (d) each work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = the technician(s), Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time and Tech Time as above, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; set Service Advisor in the work order's left panel; on the line click Add Part and add a part with the Sell Price above (it must show In stock, or be ordered and received, before you can invoice). (e) clocked time: sign in as each technician in a private window > open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out; then, as Admin, the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows). (f) on each work order: on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice).
88604.custom_steps:
1. With your busy location selected, click Dashboard in the top menu and look at each of the four tiles in the top row.
  2. Hover the arrow icon beside each tile's name.
  3. Change location to ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop (profile icon > Change Location).
  4. Read the Revenue headline and supporting line.
  5. Read the Billing Efficiency headline and supporting line.
88604.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each of the four top tiles shows its name (label), a headline value, a small trend line, a date-range pill (e.g. "This Month") and an arrow icon beside the name that links to its report. A tile with fewer than two days of figures shows a dashed outline with a chart icon instead of the trend line; that is expected and covered by its own case.
  • Revenue reads "$510.00": a dollar amount with two decimals (250.00 + 260.00).
  • Revenue's supporting line reads "Parts 41% · Labor 59%", whole numbers with no decimals (210 ÷ 510 = 41.2%, so 41%; 300 ÷ 510 = 58.8%, so 59%).
  • Billing Efficiency reads "85.71%", two decimal places (3.00 ÷ 3.50 × 100).
  • Billing Efficiency's supporting line reads "3.00 Invoiced / 3.50 Clocked".

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 4. Design canvas boards 01_Opens_After and 02_Last12_After for the tile layout (arrow icon, range pill).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R1: “Each KPI tile shows a label, a headline value, a sparkline, a date-range control, and a report link.”
  • S4-R2: “The Revenue tile headline is the total revenue for the selected range, shown as a dollar amount to the cent.”
  • S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%", each percent shown as a whole number.”
  • S4-R4: “The Billing Efficiency tile headline is the billing efficiency percentage for the selected range, shown to two decimal places.”
  • S4-R5: “The Billing Efficiency tile shows a supporting line reading "{invoiced hours} Invoiced / {clocked hours} Clocked".”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R7: “The Sales by Customer tile expands to the Sales by Customer table.”
  • S6-R8: “The At Risk Customers tile expands to the At Risk Customers table. The table is ordered by each customer's trailing-twelve-month revenue, highest first, with the customer name as the tiebreaker, so the largest amount at risk reads first. The table lists every at-risk customer. A safety cap of 500 rows applies: if a workplace ever exceeds it, the table shows the first 500 in that order and says so on screen, reading "Showing 500 of N at-risk customers", while the headline still counts every one. The table never truncates silently, because a table that stops short while the headline counts more is a defect: the two then disagree.”

88601.title: Each tile shows the same figure as its matching report
88601.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) that has invoices and technician clocked time this month (one day is enough) and over the last twelve months.
  4. Your role can create a work order and an invoice in that location (Admin can).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: on the Dashboard, Revenue on This Month is above $0.00 and Technician Efficiency on This Month shows a percentage (not -). If not, create today's data first: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save; Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = Tech ShopView, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; clock time as the technician: in a second browser or a private window, on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Tech (this signs you in as Tech ShopView, a technician at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 with Time Clock on); open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; to make the time exact, as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). Then check again. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88601.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu and leave every tile on its default range.
  2. Write down the Revenue headline.
  3. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" (it opens the Sales report on the same range) and read the report's total for the invoices' subtotals at the foot of the table.
  4. Go back to the dashboard, write down the Billing Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Service Advisor Analysis report) and read the report's overall figure with all advisors selected.
  5. Go back, write down the Technician Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Efficiency report, Invoiced) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected.
  6. Go back, write down the Technician Utilization headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Utilization report) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected.
  7. Go back, write down the Sales by Customer headline, then click its arrow icon (Sales By Customer report) and read how many customers the report lists in total (e.g. the pager reads "1 - 10 of 69").
  8. Create one new invoice in the same location today: Work Orders > Create Work Order > a customer and asset > Save; in New Line add a labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO, $100 an hour, Estimated Time 1) and tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete; Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice.
  9. Within one minute, reload the dashboard and read the Revenue headline.
  10. Reload the Sales report on the same range and read its total.
88601.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Revenue equals the Sales report total exactly, to the cent.
  • Billing Efficiency equals the Service Advisor Analysis figure, Technician Efficiency equals the Technician Efficiency report figure, and Technician Utilization equals the Technician Utilization report figure, each to two decimal places.
  • Sales by Customer equals the number of customers the Sales By Customer report lists (e.g. 69 customers and "1 - 10 of 69").
  • Straight after the new invoice, both the tile and the report have gone up by the same amount (e.g. $100.00) and still agree. There is no wait, and the tile never shows an older figure than the report.
  • If any tile and its report disagree at any point, the case fails. Write both figures in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 3. Report links per the Story 10 context note.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3-N1: “If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

88606.title: The small trend line uses days, weeks, months or quarters by range length
88606.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) with invoices over the last two years (for the long custom ranges) and, for the last step only, clocked time this month on at least two days with a day without clocked time in between.
  4. You know how to set a custom range: open a tile's range pill, click a start day and an end day in the calendar, check the length shown at the bottom (e.g. "Range: 31 days"), then click Apply.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on Last Year and on This Year shows an amount above $0.00; then set it back to This Month (the dashboard remembers your choices). For the last step: Reports > Timesheet Activities, Date Range: This month, shows clocked time on at least two days with a day without in between; if no location has that, mark only that check Blocked and write in the result comment that no such month data exists. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88606.custom_steps:
1. On the Revenue tile, pick a custom range of exactly 31 days ending today and count the points (corners) on the trend line.
  2. Change it to a custom range of exactly 32 days and count the points.
  3. Change it to exactly 182 days, then exactly 183 days, counting the points each time.
  4. Change it to exactly 731 days, then exactly 732 days, counting the points each time.
  5. Set Revenue to Last 12 Months and click View details. Compare the trend line's shape with the monthly bars in the Revenue chart.
  6. On the Billing Efficiency tile pick This Month and look at a day when nobody clocked any time (e.g. a Sunday).
88606.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • 31 days draws one point per day (up to 31 points). 32 days switches to one point per week (about 5 points).
  • 182 days still draws one point per week (about 26 points). 183 days switches to one point per month (about 7 points).
  • 731 days still draws one point per month (about 25 points). 732 days switches to one point per quarter (about 9 points).
  • On Last 12 Months the Revenue trend line has 12 points, and they rise and fall exactly like the 12 monthly bars in the expanded Revenue chart. A point never disagrees with the chart for the same month.
  • On the day with no clocked time, the Billing Efficiency line has a gap: it breaks and resumes. It is not drawn down to zero and the days either side are not joined across the gap.
  • When fewer than two points have a value, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart outline instead (checked in detail in its own cases).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 4. Design canvas board 03_Range_After (row 3) for the range pill and calendar; board 04_Revenue_After for the expanded Revenue chart; board 15_Empty_Design (row 15) for the empty-chart outline.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R10: “The sparkline shows the tile's measure trending over the selected range.”
  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
